It is NOT the S4 step-5 source lifecycle, and not the `source_lifecycle` / `source_add_battery` decision classes in common.schema.json - those are about a retrieved WORK's place in the evidence base (add / keep / supersede / coexist / quarantine / link-duplicate). Different subject, different owner, different vocabulary; docs/gen2/SOURCE-GOVERNANCE.md keeps the two apart deliberately
title: Research source proposal
description: An agent's typed proposal that the gateway should be able to call a provider it currently cannot. It authorizes nothing: it is generation, not selection (flow §2 - a new option is always a proposal to the operator), and the pathway it enters is in docs/gen2/SOURCE-GOVERNANCE.md. The document deliberately has no field for approval, for enablement, for a verified rate limit, or for a credential value: an agent cannot approve a source, cannot turn one on, cannot assert that a limit was confirmed, and cannot carry a secret. Everything the agent could not establish goes in `unknowns` rather than being filled in plausibly.

topic_id.description: The topic whose work motivated the proposal. A proposal always comes from doing research, not from browsing what exists.

motivation.description: Why this provider, tied to the record rather than to an impression. A coverage gap is stated in the gateway's own vocabulary: a lane that was `searched_ok` and returned little is a different fact from a lane that does not exist, and neither is `searched_empty`.

observed_coverage.description: What the existing lanes actually reported while the gap was observed, per lane, in the gateway's coverage vocabulary.

suggested_registry_id.description: The id the registry row would use if the proposal is approved. Lower-case with underscores, matching the registry's existing ids (`harvard_dataverse`, `api_data_gov`); the operator may change it, and nothing downstream depends on the suggestion.

provides.description: What the provider holds and what the gateway would ask it for, in the registry's own vocabulary so an approved proposal maps onto a row without translation.

allOf.description: A manual-only source is documented and never queried, so it declares no gateway capability (the registry's own rule).
Anything the gateway would call has to say what it would be called for.

placement.description: Where the provider would sit in the gateway's existing structure. A base lane is queried for every request of its kind; a domain lane is added only for the domains it is tagged with (and an `other`-domain request includes every domain lane). A substitution family groups providers that answer the same question, so the router can fall back within it. Proposing a base lane is a bigger claim than proposing a domain lane, and the rationale is where that claim is made.

expected_overlap.description: What the proposal expects this lane to duplicate. A provider with near-total overlap with an existing lane is a fallback, not a discovery lane — the registry already records one such case (OpenAIRE, 96-99% overlap with Crossref, kept as a fallback and not as a lane).

access.description: How a deployment would authenticate. `secret_ref` is a LOGICAL NAME ONLY — the value never appears in this document, and there is no field it could appear in. The auth vocabulary is the registry's, and the required/absent pairing with `secret_ref` matches what tools/gen_source_catalog.py enforces, so an approved proposal cannot produce a registry row whose keys the generator would refuse.

key_acquisition.description: The steps a person follows to obtain the credential, in enough detail to be followed — this becomes the registry row's key_instructions and then the catalog's 'How to get access'.

credential_cost.description: What obtaining it costs, as far as the provider's own pages say: no_credential, free_registration, paid, or unknown. `unknown` is a legitimate answer and is listed in `unknowns`; a guess is not.

allOf.description: An auth kind that reads a credential needs a logical name for it.
An auth kind that reads no credential must not name one: a stray secret name is how a key silently goes missing from, or is invented in, the generated .env example.
No credential to obtain, nothing to charge for.

api_shape.description: Enough of the interface to judge whether an adapter is a small job or a subsystem. Rate limits are either DOCUMENTED with the page they were read from, or undocumented and said to be so — there is no shape in which a limit can be asserted without a source, and no shape in which this document can claim a limit was verified against live headers. Verification happens later, by a person running the smoke, and is recorded in the registry seed, not here.

response_shape.description: What a successful response looks like, and — the field that matters for the gateway's repaired defect — what an error or empty result looks like, so an adapter can tell them apart instead of turning an unreadable payload into zero results.

licensing.description: The terms, read rather than assumed. `licensing_tier` is the registry's commercial verdict vocabulary, and `unknown` fails closed for commercial-flagged requests exactly as it does for an existing source. Redistribution is recorded separately because it is a different question from commercial use, and because it decides whether retrieved content may travel in an export bundle at all (docs/gen2/EXPORT-SINKS.md §2). Evidence is a link to the terms that were read: at least one, always.

allOf.description: Saying content may be redistributed means naming the licence that says so.
An unlocatable commercial verdict cannot come with a confident redistribution answer: if the terms could not be found, neither question was answered.

unknowns.description: Everything the proposal could not establish, one entry each, naming the field it is about. Present and possibly empty — an empty array is a claim that nothing was left open, which a reviewer can check against the rest of the document. A field that is `unknown` above and absent here is an inconsistency a reviewer should catch; the schema requires the array, not the cross-check.

supersedes_proposal_id.description: A previous proposal for the same provider that this one replaces (a re-proposal after a rejection is explicit, and carries what changed). An operator's rejection of the earlier proposal stands as its own record; this field does not reopen it.
